The model has one free joint and 29 hinge joints (36 qpos, 35 dof) and 29 motor actuators with ctrlranges; the bridge derives action.ctrl's per-actuator bounds from those ctrlranges (legs at g1_29dof_rev_1_0.xml:391-402, waist at :403-405, arms at :406-419), so the package writes no Limit of its own. The fake backend is fake.py, a callable stand-in mujoco module that parses the same MJCF and integrates a placeholder first-order motion. The gate warns G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND and G8.NO_UNIT x3 (seed, ticks and action.ctrl[*] are family-derived inputs); G4 had no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warning. The lock backends are documented as .fake:FakeMujoco even though driver.py names the class object, the form the SDK's own MuJoCo tests use. NOT COVERED: the MuJoCo engine was not installed and was never run, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result; the stand-in computes no inertias, contacts, friction, actuator or sensor dynamics and loads none of the 33 mesh STL files; models[0] is a bare robot asset with a free-floating base and no floor, arena or camera, and the upstream environments compose it with a separate ground arena; the three-finger hands are separate MJCF fragments attached as grippers and their seven position actuators per hand are not part of this world; the four IMU sensors are not exposed; the card's RoboSuite environment task, object, randomization and success logic is not modelled; no rendering is served; no physical G1 is modelled and no hardware run is claimed. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json authored_by is the model, reviewed_by is null).
